system.coherence.analysisDialogMessage: Analyzes whether the console's engines and modules use each other coherently (dependency graph + code reading with Sonnet) and proposes wiring/deduplication.\n\nRuns decoupled (survives restarts) and CONSUMES TOKENS. Nothing is applied automatically: you approve each proposal.
system.coherence.applyPromptIntro: The console's Coherence Module (Claude Web Console) detected that two parts of the system are not using each other optimally and proposed this wiring. Apply it under supervision.
system.coherence.applyRule1: 1. Read the root CLAUDE.md BEFORE touching anything: the hard rules (1-9) are inviolable — especially the two-layer read-only guardrail for headless runs and the decoupled runners (golden rule).
system.coherence.applyRule2: 2. Verify by reading the code that the inconsistency is still valid, that the proposed wiring is correct, and that it does not break anything else. If it does not apply, tell me and do not touch anything.
system.coherence.applyRule3: 3. ALWAYS prefer reusing the existing canonical source/service instead of duplicating logic.
system.coherence.applyRule4: 4. Check every .js file you edit with `node --check`.
system.coherence.applyRule5: 5. STOP and ask me for confirmation BEFORE any high-risk action (git push, restarting the service, deleting data).
system.coherence.applyRule6: 6. When finished, summarize what you wired, in which files, and how to verify it.
system.coherence.applyRule7: 7. As the LAST step, after verifying the change, run:\n   node bin/cwc-health-proposal-done.js {padRef}
system.coherence.resolvePromptIntro: The console's Coherence Module (Claude Web Console) detected this structural inconsistency (deterministic scan). Resolve it under supervision.
system.coherence.resolveRule1: 1. Read the root CLAUDE.md BEFORE touching anything: the hard rules (1-9) are inviolable (two-layer read-only guardrail, decoupled runners, ZeroTier bind…).
system.coherence.resolveRule2: 2. Verify by reading the code that the inconsistency is still valid. If it is a FALSE POSITIVE (e.g. a helper module that should not be mounted, or a dynamically referenced runner), tell me and do not touch anything.
system.coherence.resolveRule6: 6. When finished, summarize what you changed, in which files, and how to verify it.
system.coherence.flowPromptIntro: The console's Coherence Module (Claude Web Console) proposed this NEW FLOW to improve how engines/modules use each other. Explore the design in plan mode: evaluate whether it is worth it, how it fits the architecture (decoupled runners, golden rule, rule 6 of CLAUDE.md), and build the implementation plan. DO NOT implement anything yet.

system.optimize.applyPromptIntro: The console AI Optimization (Claude Web Console) proposed this improvement for an AI engine. Apply it under supervision.
system.optimize.applyRule1: 1. Read the root CLAUDE.md BEFORE touching anything: the hard rules (1-9) are inviolable — especially the two-layer read-only shield for headless runs and detached runners.
system.optimize.applyRule2: 2. Verify by reading the code that the proposal is still current and correct. If it does not apply, tell me and do not touch anything.
system.optimize.applyRule3: 3. Verify every .js file you edit with `node --check`.
system.optimize.applyRule4: 4. STOP and ask me for confirmation BEFORE any high-risk action (git push, restarting the service, deleting data).

system.optimize.flowPromptIntro: The console AI Optimization (Claude Web Console) proposed this NEW FLOW. Explore the design in plan mode: evaluate whether it is worthwhile, how it fits the architecture (detached runners, golden rule, rule 6 of CLAUDE.md), and build the implementation plan. system.healthReview.fullAnalysisMessage: Re-audit ALL modules from scratch (ignore the cache). Module by module with Claude. Takes several minutes and USES MORE TOKENS. Read-only.
system.healthReview.changeAnalysisMessag: Audit ONLY the modules that changed since the last review (unchanged ones are reused from the cache). Fast and inexpensive. Read-only.
system.healthReview.resolveRule1: 1. Verify by reading the cited code that the finding is REAL (the audit may be wrong). If it is a false positive, tell me and do not touch anything.
system.healthReview.resolveRule2: 2. Implement the MINIMAL fix. You may edit files directly (you are in Accept edits mode).
system.healthReview.resolveRule3: 3. STOP and ask me for confirmation BEFORE any HIGH-RISK action: deleting data, git push, restarting services, destructive commands (rm, kill, systemctl...). Do not run them without my OK.
system.healthReview.resolveRule4: 4. When finished, summarize what you changed, in which files, and how to verify it.
system.healthReview.resolvePromptIntro: Console Health Review (Claude Web Console) detected this finding. Resolve it autonomously.
system.healthReview.resolveRule5Importan: 5. IMPORTANT — when you have finished and VERIFIED the fix, mark this finding as resolved in the Health board by running EXACTLY (I will ask you for OK for the command):
system.healthReview.resolveCommand: node bin/cwc-health-resolve.js {id} "<short summary of what you fixed>"
system.healthReview.resolveCommandCautio: Do this ONLY if you really resolved it. If it turned out to be a false positive or you could not fix it, DO NOT run that command and tell me.
system.healthReview.resolveAllDialogMess:
ONE chat will open and resolve the {count} finding(s) one by one, editing the console code autonomously (Accept edits mode). It will stop and ask you for confirmation for each high-risk decision.

You can watch it live and stop it whenever you want.
system.healthReview.resolveAllPromptIntr: The console Health Review (Claude Web Console) found {count} finding(s). Resolve them autonomously, ONE BY ONE, in list order (highest severity to lowest).
system.healthReview.resolveAllSequential: Work sequentially: verify, fix, and move on to the next one. Report when each one is done and provide a final summary of everything changed.
system.healthReview.resolveAllImportant: IMPORTANT — as soon as you finish and VERIFY each finding, mark it as resolved in the Health board by running EXACTLY (I will ask you for OK for the command), using the id shown in the list above:
system.healthReview.resolveAllCommand: node bin/cwc-health-resolve.js <id> "<short summary of what you fixed>"
system.healthReview.resolveAllCaution: Do this for EACH finding you really resolved. If any one is a false positive or you could not fix it, DO NOT mark it and tell me.
system.healthReview.markResolvedMessage: Mark "{area}" as resolved? This does not touch code: it only removes it from the "unresolved" list and records it as resolved. Use it if you already fixed it (e.g. in a chat).

system.healthReview.resolveSafeMessage:
The {count} NON-critical findings are resolved autonomously: each one in its own isolated sandbox IN PARALLEL, and then they are integrated into the code ONE BY ONE with node --check (conflicting ones are left unapplied). It does NOT restart the service — you review with git and restart it yourself.

Critical findings are NOT included (they only go through "In chat").
